story_assessments.story_title: AI is pushing workers beyond their original job descriptions
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators sending client-facing work with AI help
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want AI to help them cover more client work without sending something they should have checked themselves.
story_assessments.interest_signal: OpenAI says a large share of work-related messages cross into tasks associated with another occupation.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It turns AI into a familiar client-work problem: what was drafted, what was verified, and who still owns the send.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A simple check before work leaves your hands.
story_assessments.proof_point: OpenAI says an analysis of more than 800,000 messages found 16.8% of work-related messages and 43.5% of occupation-specific messages were about tasks associated with another occupation.
search_phrases: what to verify before sending AI work
story_assessments.score_reason: This is the most directly useful story for freelancers and solo operators because it names a real work situation, shows a clear consequence, and gives a simple verification habit.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence points to AI use crossing role boundaries, which creates a pre-send checking problem before client-facing work goes out.

story_assessments.story_title: OpenAI is packaging enterprise agents as a managed work product
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators testing AI in live workflows that touch clients or records
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want AI to do more than draft, but they still need a clear human approval step before anything touches live work.
story_assessments.interest_signal: OpenAI says Presence is available today for voice and chat agents with policies, guardrails and escalation rules.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It explains the next workflow question in ordinary language: what can the system do on its own, and what still needs a person.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A clearer handoff between draft, approval and send.
story_assessments.proof_point: OpenAI says Presence is available today and is designed to help enterprises deploy trusted AI agents across customer and internal workflows with policies, guardrails and escalation rules.
story_assessments.score_reason: The story is practical and clear, especially for anyone turning AI from a draft tool into a live workflow with approvals.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence explicitly centers approved actions, policies, guardrails and escalation rules in a live workflow, which maps to a handoff problem.

story_assessments.story_title: Google is treating AI security as an authorization problem
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who let AI touch live tools, accounts or publishing steps
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want AI to be useful without giving it more access than it needs.
story_assessments.interest_signal: Google says Beyond Zero is a risk-based authorization model for AI-era security.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It signals that AI access is becoming action-by-action instead of all-or-nothing.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A simple way to think about whether an AI tool should be allowed to do a specific action.
story_assessments.proof_point: Google says Beyond Zero is a contextual, risk-based authorization model built to secure both humans and agents at the level of individual actions and resources.
search_phrases: can AI take actions in tools
story_assessments.score_reason: Useful and timely, but the evidence is more enterprise-security oriented than the fixed freelancer audience needs for a fast social explanation.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The evidence is about access control and authorization, but it is not a direct pre-send or pre-publication checking problem for the audience.

story_assessments.story_title: IBM’s CodeAlchemy shows coding AI now depends on data pipelines, not just models
story_assessments.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators who use AI to help write code
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want coding help that is dependable, not just clever.
story_assessments.interest_signal: IBM says CodeAlchemy is a nearly 1 trillion-token synthetic code dataset across 15 languages.
story_assessments.stop_reason: It is credible and technical, but it speaks more to coding infrastructure than to a broad client-work check.
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A reminder to treat data quality and test setup as part of the tool choice.
story_assessments.proof_point: IBM says CodeAlchemy is a synthetic code dataset of nearly 1 trillion tokens across 15 programming languages, released with the recipes used to create it.
story_assessments.score_reason: Interesting for coders, but less useful for the fixed audience and harder to explain as a quick, practical social post.
story_assessments.release_gate_reason: The verified evidence is about training data and coding infrastructure, not a handoff, disclosure or pre-send checking problem.

tiktok.story_title: AI is pushing workers beyond their original job descriptions
tiktok.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators using AI for client-facing or public work
tiktok.payoff: AI can cross roles, so a draft can slip through. Check what you verified before sending. Clearforge AI Output Release Gate is linked in bio.
tiktok.selection_reason: This is the strongest three-second hook for the fixed audience because it starts with client work, names the consequence immediately, and gives one simple check with a direct next step.

youtube.story_title: OpenAI is packaging enterprise agents as a managed work product
youtube.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators using AI for client-facing or public work
youtube.opening: If AI helps with client messages, invoices, or scheduling, the risky part is the handoff.
youtube.payoff: OpenAI says Presence is available today. Check who approves it before anything goes out.
youtube.selection_reason: This story fits a slightly longer explanation because it teaches the difference between a draft tool and a live workflow in plain language.

facebook.story_title: AI is pushing workers beyond their original job descriptions
facebook.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators using AI for client-facing or public work
facebook.opening: If you use AI to help with client work, the main problem is usually not the first draft.
facebook.payoff: It is the moment you send something before you have checked what changed and who should own the final step. OpenAI says work is crossing job boundaries, so make the handoff visible before it goes out. Save this for later.
facebook.selection_reason: The post sounds like one helpful person explaining a familiar client-work mistake and gives a plain-language check people can actually use.

pinterest.story_title: AI is pushing workers beyond their original job descriptions
pinterest.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators using AI for client-facing or public work
pinterest.opening: Before you send AI-assisted client work, check the handoff.
pinterest.payoff: Ask what AI drafted, what you verified, and whether a human should review it before it goes out. Save this for client emails, posts, and notes.
pinterest.selection_reason: Pinterest rewards a searchable how-to answer, and this story converts cleanly into a simple check people can save and return to later.

linkedin.story_title: OpenAI is packaging enterprise agents as a managed work product
linkedin.target_audience: Freelancers and solo operators using AI for client-facing or public work
linkedin.opening: If AI will touch client messages, invoices, or scheduling, the useful question is not whether it can do it.
linkedin.payoff: It is what has to happen before it sends. OpenAI says Presence is built with approved actions, guardrails, and escalation to people when needed. The practical lesson is simple: define one human check before AI can move anything into a live system. Save this if you are mapping a workflow.
linkedin.selection_reason: This is the cleanest LinkedIn angle because it turns the product shift into a workplace lesson about approvals, handoff points and live-system responsibility.

overall_reasoning: Story 0 is the strongest public-facing hook because it speaks directly to freelancers and solo operators sending work to clients, and it gives one simple pre-send check. Story 1 is the best follow-up for YouTube Shorts and LinkedIn because it explains managed workflows, approvals and escalation in plain workplace language. Story 2 is useful but too enterprise-security-specific for the fixed audience, and story 3 is too coding-specific to carry the edition on social. The selected assets keep to one audience, one familiar situation, one consequence, one check and one next step.
